components.name: Choice Card
components.description: Chosen card: primary border plus check box.
components.css: .ds-choice{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:.625rem;padding:.625rem .75rem;background:var(--scribe-section-background);border:1px solid var(--scribe-border-color);border-radius:var(--scribe-radius-lg,10px);font:.875rem Inter,system-ui,sans-serif;color:var(--scribe-doc-foreground)}.ds-choice small{font-size:.75rem;color:var(--scribe-muted-foreground)}.ds-choice.selected{border-color:var(--scribe-primary);outline:1px solid var(--scribe-primary)}.ds-tile{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;width:2rem;height:2rem;border-radius:var(--scribe-radius-md,8px);color:var(--scribe-type-string);background:color-mix(in oklab,var(--scribe-type-string) 10%,var(--scribe-section-background));border:1px solid color-mix(in oklab,var(--scribe-type-string) 22%,var(--scribe-section-background))}.ds-check{margin-left:auto;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;width:1.125rem;height:1.125rem;border:1px solid var(--scribe-primary);border-radius:var(--scribe-radius-sm,6px);background:var(--scribe-primary);color:var(--scribe-primary-foreground);font-size:.7rem}

components.name: Bound-value Chip
components.description: Signature: a bound value drawn like a calendar event chip.

components.name: Type Pill
components.description: Data type label tinted by data-type.
components.css: .ds-pill{--tile:var(--scribe-type-number);display:inline-flex;align-items:center;height:1.25rem;padding:0 .5rem;border-radius:999px;color:color-mix(in oklab,var(--tile) 60%,var(--scribe-doc-foreground));background:color-mix(in oklab,var(--tile) 11%,var(--scribe-section-background));border:1px solid color-mix(in oklab,var(--tile) 22%,var(--scribe-section-background));font:600 .6875rem/1 Inter,system-ui,sans-serif}

narrative.overview: Scribe is a document editor that lives inside someone else's SaaS product, so it behaves like a well-mannered guest: a light grey desk, white section cards with 1px hairlines and a barely-there shadow, a blue primary (solid for actions, a soft wash for chosen toggles), and the same blue as the accent for selection, focus and data. Every dialog, row, panel and chip reuses the same card, row and tile language, so the host and Scribe read as one app.
keyCharacteristics: Desk plus white cards, hairlines instead of heavy shadow.
Blue primary for actions (solid) and chosen state (soft wash); the accent for the canvas and for data.
One tile system marks every data type: tinted fill, tinted hairline, saturated glyph.
Light and dark themes through the same token names.

rules.name: The Public Token Rule
rules.body: Tokens are public API. Hosts set the base tokens; derived tokens are color-mix of base tokens and are never hand-set.

rules.name: The Two Selection Languages Rule
rules.body: Chosen cards and rows select with a primary (blue) border, an accent wash and a check box; the canvas selects with the blue accent ring. Intentional split.

rules.name: The No Hard-Coded Colour Rule
rules.body: No hex, rgb() or oklch() in components; use a token or a mix of tokens.

rules.name: The Label Is The Label Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracked text is only the label of a field or group, never a kicker above a heading.

rules.name: The Float Only Rule
rules.body: Hairlines carry structure; shadow-float is only for layers that sit above the page.

dos: Do keep every colour a token or a color-mix of tokens, and give new base tokens a .dark value.
Do select chosen cards and rows with the primary border plus .scribe-check, and the canvas with the accent ring.
Do mark data types with .scribe-tile / .scribe-pill and data-type.
Do give every control a visible focus state and an accessible name.
Do keep transitions to 150ms ease-out and honour prefers-reduced-motion.
donts: Don't use coloured pills for data types outside the tile system.
Don't use shadows for structure; hairlines do that.
Don't put Tailwind or monospace into src/lib.
Don't use floating labels or placeholder-as-label; the label sits above the field.
Don't use uppercase tracked text as a kicker above headings.
